proposals.after: He was a man of Jiexiu in Taiyuan commandery.

proposals.before: When he first met Commandant of Henan Li Ying, Ying thought him extraordinary; they became close friends, and thereafter his name shook the capital.
proposals.after: When he first met Governor of Henan Li Ying, Ying thought him extraordinary; they became close friends, and thereafter his name shook the capital.
proposals.reason: 河南尹 is the governor of Henan, not a commandant.

proposals.before: Liu Xiang's Xin Xu tells how Marquis Wen of Wei bowed from his chariot at Duan Ganmu's lane, granted him a vast stipend, and called on him often.
proposals.after: The Xin Xu tells how Marquis Wen of Wei bowed from his chariot at Duan Ganmu's lane, granted him a vast stipend, and called on him often.
proposals.reason: Chinese names only 《新序》, not Liu Xiang; the idiomatic English invents an author not in this unit.

proposals.before: When Qin planned to strike Wei, Sima Tang objected: "Everyone knows Wei honors the worthy Duan Ganmu—surely this is no time to march."』
proposals.after: When Qin planned to strike Wei, Sima Tang objected: "Duan Ganmu is a worthy man, and Wei treats him with ceremony—the whole world has heard of it; is it not perhaps impermissible to apply arms?"
proposals.reason: Idiomatic 無乃不可加兵乎 is inverted into 'no time to march' and drops the worthiness/ceremony logic of the remonstrance.

proposals.before: 〈(The Analects: Qu Boyu's messenger asks Confucius's disciple, 『What has the Master been up to?』
proposals.after: 〈(The Analects: Qu Boyu sent a man to Confucius, who asked him, 『What has the Master been doing?』
proposals.reason: Chinese is 蘧伯玉使人於孔子，問之曰: Confucius questions the messenger about Qu Boyu; the idiomatic version wrongly makes the messenger ask Confucius's disciple.

proposals.before: He answered: "To heap scorn on the unworthy only deepens the trouble—that is what Confucius meant."
proposals.after: He answered: "If a person is not humane, to hate him to excess is to bring disorder."
proposals.reason: The unit quotes Analects 人而不仁，疾之以甚，亂也; Confucius is identified only in the following note, and 'that is what Confucius meant' is invented.

proposals.before: He won a reputation for stern integrity, entered the central administration, rose to attendant censor and governor of Bing, and left a record of moral sway wherever he served.
proposals.after: He won a reputation for stern integrity, entered the central administration, rose to attendant censor and inspector of Bing, and left a record of moral sway wherever he served.
proposals.reason: 刺史 is provincial inspector, not commandery governor; the idiomatic 'governor of Bing' misrenders the office.

proposals.before: 〈(Xie Cheng: "Jia Shu had avenged his uncle Song Yuan in town, been arrested, and faced the death cell—
proposals.after: 〈(Xie Cheng: "Jia Shu had avenged his maternal uncle Song Yuan in town, been arrested, and faced the death cell—
proposals.reason: 舅 is specifically maternal uncle; 'uncle' erases the maternal line the feud depends on.

proposals.before: Xie Zhen (distinct from the historian Xie Cheng), courtesy name Ziwei, hailed from Shaoling in Runan.
proposals.after: Xie Zhen, courtesy name Ziwei, hailed from Shaoling in Runan.
proposals.reason: The parenthetical contrast with historian Xie Cheng is not in the Chinese and is an inserted identification, not a translation of 謝甄字子微.

proposals.before: Young Lord Shao and Xu Weikang both came out of butchery and liquor-selling; Sima Ziwei was raised from the ranks; together with Guo Changxin, Wang Changwen, Han Wenbu, Li Zizheng, Cao Ziyuan of the same commandery, Zhou Kangzi of Dingxiang, Wang Jiran of Xihe, Qiu Jizhi of Yunzhong, Hao Lizhen, and others—sixty men in all—all became established in reputation.
proposals.after: Shao Gongzi and Xu Weikang both came out of butchery and liquor-selling; Sima Ziwei was raised from the ranks; together with Guo Changxin, Wang Changwen, Han Wenbu, Li Zizheng, Cao Ziyuan of the same commandery, Zhou Kangzi of Dingxiang, Wang Jiran of Xihe, Qiu Jizhi of Yunzhong, Hao Lizhen, and others—sixty men in all—all became established in reputation.
proposals.reason: 召公子 is a personal name Shao Gongzi, not the title Young Lord Shao (which would imply the Zhou founder 召公).

proposals.before: Zishi reached the ministry, Jiran governed Beidi, most of the rest held regional office.")〉
proposals.after: Zishi rose to Minister of Education; Jiran became Governor of Beidi; most of the rest held provinces and commanderies.")〉
proposals.reason: 司徒 is the specific office Minister of Education, not a generic ministry.

proposals.before: Courteous and good at guiding, causing scholars to yearn to establish a name—even followers of Mo and Meng could not surpass him.
proposals.after: Courteous and good at guiding, causing scholars to yearn to establish a name—even Mozi and Mencius could not surpass him.
proposals.reason: The commentary (s0197) glosses 墨、孟之徒 as 墨翟、孟軻 themselves, not their later followers.

proposals.before: 〈(According to the Xu Han zhi, the capital "metropolitan investigator" policed wrongdoing among the bureaucracy."
proposals.after: 〈(According to the Xu Han zhi, the metropolitan investigator policed wrongdoing among the bureaucracy.)
proposals.reason: Stray closing quote and wording that treats Xu Han as a person-like capital epithet; the note cites 續漢志 on the office 都官從事.

proposals.before: Li Ying received Guo Tai as equal and mentor, and Guo's reputation shook the realm—that was Fu Rong's doing.")〉
proposals.after: Li Ying received Guo Tai with the rites due to a teacher and friend, and Guo's reputation shook the realm—that was Fu Rong's doing.")〉
proposals.reason: 師友之禮 is the etiquette of teacher-and-friend, not 'equal and mentor'.

proposals.before: Rong went once and recommended and advanced three commandery scholars—Fan Ran, Han Zhuo, Kong Zhou, and others,
proposals.after: Rong went once and recommended and advanced three commandery scholars—Fan Ran, Han Zhuo, and Kong Zhou.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 等三人 names exactly those three men; 'and others' invents extra people.

proposals.before: Xu Shao's kinsmen Xu Jing, Xu Xun, and Xu Xiang had all reached the three highest posts; Xu Xiang had curried favor with the eunuchs to get there and repeatedly summoned Xu Shao to court.
proposals.after: Xu Shao's great-uncle Jing, Jing's son Xun, and Xun's son Xiang had all reached the three highest posts; Xiang, because he could flatter the eunuchs, reached the high offices and was enfeoffed as a marquis, and repeatedly sent to invite Shao.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line flattens 從祖敬，敬子訓，訓子相 into three equal kinsmen and drops the great-uncle/son/grandson genealogy and Xiang's enfeoffment.

proposals.before: He spurned Minister Yang Biao, the recommendations for upright and plain virtue, and imperial summons.
proposals.after: The Minister of Works Yang Biao summoned him; he was recommended for upright and plain virtue and received an imperial summons, but he accepted none of these.
proposals.reason: 辟 is Yang Biao summoning Xu Shao, not Xu Shao spurning Yang Biao; 皆不就 covers the summons and the recommendations together.

proposals.before: When Sun Ce pacified Wu, Shao and Yao fled south to Yuzhang and died; he was forty-six years old at the time.
proposals.after: When Sun Ce pacified Wu, Shao fled south to Yuzhang with Yao and died; he was forty-six years old at the time.
proposals.reason: 而卒 and 時年四十六 belong to the biography's subject Xu Shao, not to both Shao and Yao.

proposals.before: The Palace edition reads "nao" (stir) for "rao"; Yiwen leiju 72 agrees with the Xu Hanshu quotation.
proposals.after: The Palace edition reads "nao" (stir) for "rao"; Taiping Yulan 72 cites the Xu Hanshu the same way.
proposals.reason: 御覽 is the Taiping Yulan, not Yiwen leiju.
